Farmisi Khatun ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Md Yasin Degree College and others ----- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Plaintiff-petitioner on presentation of a petition under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly, the Code) seeks Review of a judgment dated 28-2-2007, recorded by this Court in Civil Revision No. 5049 of 2004, discharging the Rule arising out of the judgment and order dated 9-11-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Pabna, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 18 of 2004, affirming those of dated 25-4-2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pabna, in Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003, rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

 4. On 27-10-2003 the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 72 of 2003, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Pabna, impleading the opposite parties as defendants for declaration that the letter dated 18-10-2003 issued under the signature of Chairman of the Government Body of Md Yasin Degree College (opposite party No. 1) suspending the petitioner from the post of Assistant Professor Psychology Department is illegal, without jurisdiction, void and not binding upon the petitioner. On the same date, the plaintiff also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code for temporary injunction for restraining the defendant— 

 6. Plaintiff-petitioner felt dissatisfied of the above adjudication of the matter and invoked this Court's Provisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code on presentation of Revision Petition and obtained the Rule. Revision Petition had been numbered as Civil Revision No. 5049 of 2004. After hearing, this Court by the judgment and order dated 28-2-2007 discharged the Rule on the following grounds: 

 "On consideration of the materials on record, I find that the order of suspension was for a temporary period and the final order was not passed. Therefore, I hold that the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. Both the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff has no prima facie case and the application for temporary injunction was pre-mature. I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent views." 

 In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles. Moreover, the trial Court directed the concerned authority of the College to pay 50% of the Government allowance to the plaintiff. It further appears that the Courts below concurrently held that the plaintiff will not suffer any irreparable loss or injury by the impugned decision of the College. Moreover, no final order has yet been passed against the plaintiff. I am also in agreement with the aforesaid concurrent views of the Courts below." 

 "Suspension of an employee pending a disciplinary proceeding is an approved measure and the Court does not generally interfere with it. But if the order of suspension is prima facie illegal and tinged with mala fide, the Court is competent to act for preventing injustice. 

 9. The learned Counsel lastly submits that in view of the aforesaid facts the petitioner established a prima facie case for obtaining an order or temporary injunction and, as such, the judgment and order dated 28-2-2007 passed by this Court may be reviewed. 

 First, the plaintiff has to establish a prima facie case. Secondly, it was to be shown that the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted and thirdly, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff and in favour of granting the temporary injunction prayed for." 

 In the instant case, the plaintiff failed to show any one of the aforesaid principles and, as such, she is not entitled to get an order of temporary injunction.
